wblra_section_21b.short_citation: Section 21B of the West Bengal Land Reforms Act, 1955 (statutory presumption of bargadar cultivation).
wblra_section_21b.verified_against: PRS India copy of the West Bengal Land Reforms Act, 1955 (law student); independently corroborated against Indian Kanoon text on 2026-10-25.
wblra_section_21b.verbatim_section_text: 21B. Person cultivating land of another person to be presumed to be a bargadar in certain cases.—A person lawfully cultivating any land belonging to another person shall be presumed to be a bargadar in respect of such land if such person is not a member of the family of the other person whose land he cultivates and the burden of proving that such person is not a bargadar or that the land is in his personal cultivation shall, notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in any other law for the time being in force, lie on the person who alleges that the person cultivating the land is not a bargadar in respect of such land.
wblra_section_21b.insertion_history: Inserted by the West Bengal Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1969 (West Ben. Act XI of 1969).
wblra_section_21b.insertion_history_status: VERIFIED_PRIMARY (per law student, PRS India copy footnote)
applicability_conditions: The person must be lawfully cultivating land belonging to another person.
The person must not be a member of the family of the landowner.
wblra_section_21b.crop_share_rule_note: Crop-share is not a fixed constant under the Act; it depends on who supplies the inputs. The field stays blank unless entered and verified.

bsa_section_63_4.short_citation: Section 63(4) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023 (Part A & Part B of The Schedule).
bsa_section_63_4.part_a_signatory: DLSA PLV (as person in charge of the claim on the farmer's behalf).

case_reference.reported_name: Pune Bar Association v. Union of India, W.P. (C) No. 599 of 2026
case_reference.reported_holding: Upheld Section 63(4) and the Schedule; clarified that Part B need not be signed exclusively by a Section 79A notified Examiner, leaving the scope of 'expert' under Part B open.

bsa_section_63_4.footnote_text: The Supreme Court has kept the scope of 'expert' under Part B open; we conservatively designate a qualified geomatics professional.

primary_clause.text: Intimation may be given within 72 hours by the farmer either directly through the 'Crop Insurance App' or on dedicated centralized toll-free number of Krishi Rakshak Portal & Helpline (14447).

supporting_clauses.summary: Partial information may be given initially; complete details may follow within 7 days.
supporting_clauses.app_rule: The 72-hour step is the intimation only, not the full claim.

supporting_clauses.summary: Banks / government officials who receive an intimation must forward it to the insurer within 48 hours.
supporting_clauses.app_rule: If intimation is lodged through a bank or official, track a 48-hour forwarding deadline.

dpdp_act_2023.short_citation: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
dpdp_act_2023.right_to_erasure: Data Principals have the right to erasure and withdrawal of consent; data must be deleted once purpose is served.
dpdp_act_2023.delete_button_notice: Your claim data will be deleted, subject to 48-hour notice and statutory retention of security logs for one year under the DPDP Rules, 2025.
dpdp_act_2023.log_retention_rule: Rule 8(3), DPDP Rules, 2025 (released 14 November 2025): one-year minimum retention of logs for breach investigations.
dpdp_act_2023.forty_eight_hour_notice_rule: Rule 8(2), DPDP Rules, 2025: 48-hour prior notice to the Data Principal before erasing personal data.
